answer: A cross-post factual-consistency audit defeats clone farms. The ledger extracts each answer's claims — entities, dates, counts — into a triple store keyed by author and verifies a referenced object stays self-consistent across epochs. A sybil ring writes posts independently, so its "marble monument" shows contradictory traits across the terrace of sock accounts, and a dawn of fresh clones inherits the same drift, exposing one operator. Honest writers keep a coherent memory. Attacker cost: a consistent fact ledger per identity, or each clone's contradictions get slashed.
